title: SQL Fundamentals for Statistical Analysis
description: Introduces relational databases and SQL querying for officials working with survey and administrative data. Covers SELECT and filtering, sorting, aggregate functions, GROUP BY with HAVING, and the four join types, using unit-level survey tables as worked examples. Learners finish able to extract a tabulation from a schedule database without depending on a programmer.

title: Advanced SQL for Survey Data Processing
description: Builds on basic querying to cover window functions, common table expressions, self-joins and set operations as they arise in survey data processing. Works through deduplication of household rosters, longitudinal linkage across survey rounds, and consistency edits expressed as SQL constraints. Emphasis throughout is on producing reproducible query scripts rather than one-off ad hoc queries.

title: Python for Official Statistics
description: A first programming course aimed at statistical officers with no coding background. Covers Python syntax, data types, control flow, functions and file handling, then applies them to reading fixed-width and delimited survey files and producing simple frequency tables. Every exercise uses statistical data rather than generic programming puzzles.

title: Pandas and NumPy for Survey Data Pipelines
description: Teaches the pandas and NumPy stack for building repeatable survey processing pipelines. Covers merging schedules, reshaping between wide and long layouts, applying design weights, handling missing responses, and writing validation checks that fail loudly. Concludes with packaging a pipeline so a colleague can rerun the whole estimation from raw files.

title: R for Statistical Estimation and Weighting
description: Covers R for design-based estimation, with particular attention to the survey package. Learners compute weighted means, ratios and totals with correct standard errors for stratified multistage designs, and produce estimates with confidence intervals suitable for publication. Includes reproducible reporting so tables regenerate when the input data is revised.

title: Complex Survey Sampling Designs
description: Advances from simple random sampling to the stratified multistage designs used in national household surveys. Covers probability proportional to size selection, sub-sampling within first-stage units, design effects, and the construction and calibration of survey weights. Learners evaluate a real sampling design and justify its parameters against precision requirements.

title: Questionnaire Design and Field Instrument Testing
description: Covers the design of survey schedules from concept definition through question wording, response categories, skip logic and reference periods. Includes cognitive testing, pilot design and the interpretation of non-response patterns as evidence of instrument problems. Learners revise a defective schedule and document why each change was made.

title: Statistical Visualisation and Dashboards for Policy
description: Teaches chart selection, honest scaling and accessible colour for official statistical releases. Covers uncertainty representation, small multiples for state comparisons, and the construction of a policy dashboard that answers a stated question rather than displaying every available series. Includes a review clinic on charts that mislead.

title: Geospatial Foundations for Statistical Mapping
description: An introduction to geographic information systems for statistical staff. Covers coordinate reference systems, vector and raster data, administrative boundary hierarchies down to village level, and the production of choropleth maps from tabulated indicators. Learners join a district-level indicator table to a boundary layer and publish a clean map.

title: Applied Machine Learning for Administrative Data
description: Covers supervised learning methods with direct statistical office applications: automated coding of occupation and industry text, record linkage across administrative registers, and outlier detection in enterprise returns. Stresses evaluation discipline, class imbalance and the limits of prediction as a substitute for measurement. Assumes working Python.

title: Cloud Fundamentals for Government Data Platforms
description: Explains cloud service models, tenancy and shared responsibility in the context of government data platforms and MeghRaj. Covers object storage, managed databases, identity and access management, and cost control for analytical workloads. Learners map an existing on-premises statistical workflow to cloud services and identify what must not move.

title: Statistical Disclosure Control and Data Privacy
description: Covers the confidentiality obligations attaching to unit-level statistical data and the techniques that protect them. Includes identification risk assessment, cell suppression, rounding, record swapping and the preparation of public-use microdata files. Situates each technique against the legal duty of confidentiality owed to respondents.

title: SDG Indicator Framework and National Reporting
description: Introduces the global SDG indicator framework and the National Indicator Framework used for reporting in India. Covers tier classification, metadata requirements, data source mapping across ministries, and the disaggregation expected for leave-no-one-behind reporting. Learners trace one indicator from source survey to published national value.

title: Managing Statistical Projects and Survey Operations
description: Covers planning and control of survey operations from sanction through field work to release. Includes work breakdown and scheduling for field seasons, budgeting for enumerator deployment, risk registers for non-response and field disruption, and stakeholder reporting to controlling authorities. Learners build a project plan for a state-level survey round.

title: Stata for Complex Survey Analysis
description: Teaches Stata for design-based analysis of national survey data. Covers the svyset family for declaring stratification, clustering and weights, data management with merge and reshape, and do-file discipline so an estimate can be reproduced a year later. Concludes with producing publication-ready tables directly from estimation output.

title: SPSS for Survey Tabulation and Analysis
description: An introduction to SPSS for statistical staff who tabulate survey results. Covers variable and value labels, recoding and computing new variables, cross-tabulation with significance tests, and the complex samples module for design-based estimation. Emphasises writing syntax files rather than working through menus, so analysis can be repeated.

title: SAS for Large-Scale Statistical Production
description: Covers SAS as a production tool for national statistical processing. Includes the DATA step and PROC SQL, merging and summarising multi-million-record survey files, the SURVEYMEANS and SURVEYFREQ procedures, and macro programming so a survey round can be rerun without editing code. Ends with scheduling batch jobs for a release calendar.

title: APIs and Interoperability for Government Data
description: Explains how government systems exchange data through interfaces. Covers REST design, authentication and API key handling, pagination, rate limiting, schema versioning and backward compatibility, and SDMX web services for statistical exchange. Learners publish an indicator series through a documented interface and consume another ministry's.

title: Open Data and Statistical Dissemination
description: Covers the release of official statistics for public reuse under the National Data Sharing and Accessibility Policy. Includes machine-readable formats, licensing, dataset cataloguing for discoverability, revision and versioning notices, and microdata release procedure. Throughout, weighs openness against the confidentiality owed to respondents.

title: Cybersecurity for Statistical Systems
description: Addresses the security of systems holding unit-level statistical data. Covers threat modelling for a statistical office, least-privilege access control, encryption in transit and at rest, secure configuration baselines, logging and incident response, and the CERT-In reporting directions that apply to government bodies. Includes a tabletop breach exercise.

title: Digital Signatures and e-Authentication in Government
description: Explains how authenticity and non-repudiation are established in government workflows. Covers public key infrastructure, classes of digital signature certificate, the legal standing of electronic signatures under the Information Technology Act, and eSign. Learners sign and verify a statistical release and trace what a signature does and does not prove.

title: Digital Public Infrastructure and Administrative Data
description: Covers India's digital public infrastructure and its statistical implications. Includes the identity, payments and data-exchange layers, consent-based sharing through account aggregator patterns, API Setu, and the use of administrative records held in these systems as a statistical source. Examines coverage bias and governance questions that arise from doing so.

title: Communicating Statistics to Policy Audiences
description: Teaches officials to explain statistical results to readers who are not statisticians. Covers briefing notes and press releases, describing a methodology change without inviting distrust, communicating uncertainty so it is understood rather than dismissed, and responding when a published figure is misinterpreted in public debate.

title: Professional Ethics in Official Statistics
description: Grounds officials in the Fundamental Principles of Official Statistics and their practical consequences. Covers professional independence when a result is unwelcome, impartiality in choosing methods, release calendars and equal access, the duty owed to respondents, and the correct handling of an error discovered after publication. Built around real dilemmas.

title: Evidence-Based Decision Making for Administrators
description: Bridges statistical evidence and administrative decisions. Covers framing a policy question so data can answer it, reasoning under uncertainty and with incomplete evidence, separating correlation from causation in a policy argument, weighing cost against risk, and documenting the basis of a decision so it survives later review.

title: Change Management for Digital Adoption
description: Covers leading the adoption of new methods and systems in a statistical office. Includes stakeholder analysis, anticipating and addressing resistance, phased rollout of a new instrument or platform, training and support during transition, and sustaining a change once the project team has moved on. Uses the shift to computer-assisted personal interviewing as the worked case.

title: Large Language Models for Text in Official Statistics
description: Applies large language models to statistical text problems: coding free-text occupation and industry responses, classifying open-ended survey answers, and extracting structure from administrative documents. Covers prompt design, evaluation against a human-coded gold standard, hallucination risk, and why a model output must never be published without a deterministic check.

title: Big Data Processing for Statistical Workloads
description: Covers processing datasets too large for a single machine. Includes distributed storage and compute, partitioning strategies for survey and administrative data, columnar formats, and the trade-off between a big data platform and a well-indexed database. Learners move a slow national tabulation onto a distributed pipeline and measure the difference.
